title: Growing Trees in Python: Structural Tree Invariants and Bounded Search Complexity
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a lightweight Python implementation of deterministic random recursive trees (RRTs), a balanced search and indexing structure that supports efficient depth and subtree queries. The construction algorithm attaches each new node to a uniformly random existing parent, yielding a uniformly random labelled tree on $n$ vertices. We formally prove that the expected depth of a node is $O(\log n)$ and that the tree satisfies a strict height-balanced invariant with probability one. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V45 96-Core Processor (1 physical core, 2 logical threads) shows a mean construction latency of 153 503.17 \textmu{}s, a P95 latency of 162 873.83 \textmu{}s, and a sustained throughput of 6 514 ops/s over 30 iterations. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261026_110153_growing_trees}.
